notes: Checked header/footer nav (no link), sitemap.xml (1515 URLs, grepped for new|arriv|latest|just-in - no dedicated route), and direct probes for /new-arrivals, /new-arrival, /new-in, /whats-new, /just-in, /latest - all return soft-404s (Next.js notFound boundary content, same as a deliberately nonsense slug), so no standalone New Arrivals PLP/URL exists on this site. However, the homepage DOES carry a genuine, site-authored New Arrivals merchandising section: eyebrow 'Just landed', heading (h2) literally 'New Arrivals', section title 'Fresh off the workbench', and copy 'The latest fixtures to join our catalogue - be the first to light up your space with them.' This is a real product carousel (not editorial/lookbook-only): counted 50 unique, distinct PDP links (data-index 0-49 in the react-multi-carousel track, no duplicates) under this heading before the next section ('Curated for every corner') begins. This satisfies the brief's content test (real products listed; genuinely represents newly-added catalogue items, not a seasonal campaign) but NOT the PLP-URL test: the section has no 'View all' link, no own route/anchor, no pagination, and no explicit site-reported total (unlike /sale, which shows an explicit 'N products' count + pagination JSON) - so the 50 I counted is just what happens to be embedded in this homepage widget and may be an API-side cap (e.g. 'latest N=50') rather than the genuine total count of new arrivals. Backend product tag field 'websiteCategories' (checked on homepage JSON) has no 'new'/'new-arrival' value, confirming there is no backend category/tag driving this - it's a homepage-only curated widget, not a full indexed listing page. Recorded the row per the brief's guidance to record-and-flag rather than guess on a genuine ambiguous case, using the homepage as the only available link.
